LLC, Pontiac, Michigan (FA8626-27-D-B003); and Zulu Pods Inc., Amherst, Massachusetts (FA8626-27-D-B002), have been awarded a cumulative, maximum ceiling $16,100,000,000 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for advanced propulsion enterprise work. Work will be performed at each awardees location as listed above and is expected to be completed by November 2041. These contracts were competitive acquisitions. Fiscal 2027 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $58,000 ($1,000 per awardee) are obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Material Command, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity.

Chromalloy Component Services Inc., San Antonio, Texas (FA8122-27-D-B002); and Global Turbine Services Inc., Doral, Florida (FA8122-27-D-B001), were awarded a maximum $871,000,000 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, firm-fixed-price, multiple-award contract for F108 engine sustainment. This contract provides for the remanufacture of F108 low-pressure turbine module 13/15 and module 14 for the Air Force and Navy. Work will be performed at each awardee's location and is expected to be completed by Nov. 19, 2031. These contracts were competitive acquisitions, and two offers were received. The Air Force Sustainment Center, Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma, is the contracting activity.

MVP Robotics Inc., Bradford, Vermont, has been awarded a $90,100,000 firm-fixed-price modification (P00002) to a previously awarded contract (FA2280-26-D-0001) to increase the ceiling amount. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $95,000.000 from $4,900,000. Work will be performed in Bradford, Vermont, and is expected to be completed by Sep. 24, 2031. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $4,335,000 are being obligated at time of award. The AFWERX Enterprise Contracting Branch, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity.

Applied Research Associates, Albuquerque, New Mexico, has been awarded a $65,514,830 cost-plus-fixed-fee contract for optical radiation bioeffects and safety II. This contract provides for research on directed energy-based devices and systems. Work will be performed at Joint Base San Antonio-Fort Sam Houston, Texas, and is expected to be completed by Dec. 1, 2029. Fiscal 2027 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $1,234,928 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Research Laboratory, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity. (FA2384-27-C-B002).

Parsons Government Services Inc., Centreville, Virginia, has awarded a $29,754,691 firm-fixed price undefinitized contract ceiling for Integrated Solutions for Situational Awareness. This contract provides for the full range of technical sustainment and programmatic support necessary to deliver and maintain operational capabilities across multiple security domains and classification levels. Work will be performed at Los Angeles, California, and is expected to be completed by Nov. 9, 2027. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $1,125,000 at time of award. The Space Systems Command, Los Angeles Air Force Base, California, is the contracting activity (FA8806-27-C-B003). (Awarded on Oct. 28, 2026).

NAVY

Lockheed Martin Corp., Titusville, Florida, is awarded an un-priced letter contract modification (N0003026C0100P00002) with a not to exceed amount of $1,533,124,563 for TRIDENT II (D5) missile production and deployed systems support. Work will be performed in Magna, Utah (16%); Cape Canaveral, Florida (14%); Denver, Colorado (14%); Titusville, Florida (11%); Kings Bay, Georgia (8%); Culpepper, Virginia (7%); Bangor, Washington (6%); Sunnyvale, California (4%); Valley Forge; Pennsylvania (3%); Huntsville, Alabama (2%); Las Vegas, Nevada; (1%) Biddeford, Maine (1%); Elma, New York (1%); Elkton, Maryland (1%); Inglewood, California (1%); Joplin, Missouri (1%); Lancaster, Pennsylvania (1%); and various other locations (less than 1% each totaling 8%). Work is expected to be completed Sep. 30, 2031. This contract is being awarded to the contractor on a sole source basis under 10 U.S. Code 3204(a)(1) and was previously synopsized on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) online portal. Strategic Systems Programs, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity. 

The Charles Stark Draper Laboratory, Cambridge, Massachusetts, is awarded a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract modification (P00035) to a previously awarded and announced contract (N0003024C6001) in the amount of $315,687,820.  This modification adds scope to provide support for the Trident II D5 Strategic Weapons System Program. Specifically, this contract modification provides specialized engineering support for the guidance subsystem. Work will be performed in Cambridge, Massachusetts (70%); Pittsfield, Massachusetts (15%); Buffalo, New York (5%); Cape Canaveral, Florida (5%); and El Segundo, California (5%), with an expected completion date of Sept. 30, 2028. Fiscal 2027 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $315,687,820 will be obligated on this modification. No funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract is awarded as a sole-source acquisition pursuant to 10 U.S. Code 2304(c)(1) and was previously synopsized on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) online portal. Portfolio Acquisition Executive Strategic Systems Programs, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity. 

Crowley Government Services Inc., Jacksonville, Florida is awarded a $270,425,765 firm-fixed-price contract with pass-through elements (N3220527C1202) for the operation and maintenance of six government-owned Transportation Auxiliary General Ocean Surveillance (T-AGOS) and Transportation Auxiliary General Missile Range instrument (T-AGM) vessels. The vessels under this award include USNS Victorious (T-AGOS 19), USNS Able (T-AGOS 20), USNS Effective (T-AGOS 21), USNS Loyal (T-AGOS 22), USNS Impeccable (T-AGOS 23) and USNS Howard O. Lorenzen (T-AGM 25). The contract, to be performed worldwide, will consist of a six-month firm period beginning Dec. 1, 2026, to May 31, 2027, followed by one, six-month option period beginning June 1, 2027, to Nov. 30, 2027, and one six-month option (pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation 52.217-8 Option to Extend Services) beginning Dec. 1, 2027, to May 30, 2028, and will utilize fiscal 2027 working capital funds (Navy). This contract was not competitively procured, the contract was prepared under the authority of 10 U.S. Code 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Military Sealift Command, Norfolk, Virginia, is the contracting activity. 

Lockheed Martin Corp., Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Co., Fort Worth, Texas, is awarded a $72,580,901 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification (P00047) to a previously awarded contract (N0001923C0009). This modification adds scope, increasing the ceiling to provide additional program management, software engineering, software engineering transformation, and cybersecurity support required to accelerate the development of F-35 Lightning II Block 4 capabilities. Work will be performed in Fort Worth, Texas (60%); Nashua, New Hampshire (16%); Baltimore, Maryland (9%); Orlando, Florida (5.5%); El Segundo, California (2%); San Diego, California (2%); Torrance, California (2%); Buffalo, New York (1%); Clearwater, Florida (1%); Northridge, California (1%); and Tucson, Arizona (0.5%), and is expected to be completed in March 2028. No funds will be obligated at the time of award. This modification was not competitively procured. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

General Dynamics Electric Boat Corp., Groton, Connecticut, is awarded a $42,624,389 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification to a previously awarded contract (N0002420C2114) for reactor plant planning yard support for nuclear-powered submarines and support yard for the Navy’s moored training ships. Work will be performed in Groton, Connecticut (90%); and Charleston, South Carolina (10%). Fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $5,000,000 (59%); and fiscal 2027 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $3,542,500 (41%), will be obligated at time of award; and funds in the amount of $5,000,000 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

and Zolon TTS LLC, Manassas, Virginia (N6600127D0056), are awarded a combined $34,300,000 cost-plus-fixed-fee and cost-no-fee, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, multiple-award contract for operational exercise design and construction, operations and requirements analysis, concept formulation and development, feasibility demonstrations, and operational and technical support. This includes efforts to analyze and engineer operational, functional and system requirements to establish national, theater and force-level architecture. Additional efforts will include requirements verification and validation, engineering analysis, technical documentation, software and hardware design and implementation, systems integration, testing, evaluation and demonstration. Awardees will have the opportunity to compete for task orders during the ordering period. No funds will be obligated at the time of award; funds will be obligated on individual orders as they are issued. Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific, San Diego, California, is the contracting activity.

Raytheon Co., Largo, Florida, was awarded a $26,742,079 firm-fixed price, cost-plus-fixed-fee, cost-plus-incentive-fee, and cost-only modification to a previously awarded contract (N0002425C5239) to exercise options for design, development, integration, test, and maintenance of system capabilities for the design agent and engineering support efforts to the critical major weapon system, Cooperative Engagement Capabilities. This contract combines purchases for the U.S. government (53%); and the governments of Australia (24%), Japan (17%), and Canada (6%), under the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) program. Work will be performed in St. Petersburg, Florida (81%); Largo, Florida (16%); and Maynard, Massachusetts (3%), and is expected to be completed by November 2027. Fiscal 2027 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $7,250,623 (27%); FMS (Australia) funds in the amount of $6,514,456 (24%); fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $4,967,430 (18%); FMS (Japan) funds in the amount of $4,495,601 (17%); FMS (Canada) funds in the amount of $1,473,969 (6%); fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,390,000 (5%); fiscal 2027 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $500,000 (2%); and fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Marine Corps) funds in the amount of $150,000 (1%), are obligated at time of award; and funds in the amount of $6,507,430 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. PAE Mission Systems, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (Awarded Nov. 18, 2026).

KBR Services LLC, Houston, Texas, is awarded a $25,457,251 firm-fixed-price modification to a previously awarded indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract (N6247017D4007). This modification issues a second bridge for base operating support services at Naval Support Activity Bahrain. Work will be performed at the Naval Support Activity and outlying support sites in the Kingdom of Bahrain and is expected to be completed by Nov. 30, 2027. This award brings the cumulative value of the contract to $253,918,496. No funds will be obligated at the time of award of this modification; fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds will be obligated on individual task orders prior to the start of service. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Naples, Italy, is the contracting activity.

Huntington Ingalls Inc., Newport News, Virginia, was awarded a $10,142,483 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification to a previously awarded contract (N0002422C2105) for engineering and design work in support of standard Navy valves installed in nuclear-powered submarines. Work will be performed in Newport News, Virginia. Fiscal 2027 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,500,000 will be obligated at time of award and will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (Awarded Nov. 19, 2026).

Huntington Ingalls Inc., Ingalls Shipbuilding Division, Pascagoula, Mississippi, is awarded a $9,822,883 cost-plus-award fee, cost-plus-fixed fee with a special performance incentive, and cost-only modification to previously awarded contract (N0002420C4203) to exercise option year seven for the accomplishment of follow-on for CG-47 class integrated planning yard services. Huntington Ingalls Inc. will provide expert design, planning and material support services for both maintenance and modernization. Work will be performed in Pascagoula, Mississippi, and is expected to be completed by December 2027. No funding will be obligated at the time of award. This option year was not competitively procured in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulations 6.302-1 (a) (2ii), only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy the agency requirements. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

ARMY

Dynamic-HHS JV,* Winnebago, Nebraska (W91278-27-D-A004); SRM Group LLC, doing business as VWI,* Virginia Beach, Virginia (W91278-27-D-A005); Incollaborative Services LLC,* Austin, Texas (W91278-27-D-A006); Facility Services Management Inc., Clarksville, Tennessee (W91278-27-D-A007); J&J Worldwide Services, doing business as CBRE, McLean, Virginia (W91278-27-D-A008); HHS Government Services, Dripping Springs, Texas (W91278-27-D-A009); and Valiant Government Services, Herndon, Virginia (W91278-27-D-A010), will compete for each order of the $450,000,000 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for operation and maintenance with incidental repair and minor construction in support of the Defense Health Agency program in the West of the Mississippi River region. Bids were solicited via the internet with 13 received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Nov. 19, 2031. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile, Alabama, is the contracting activity.

Korte Construction Co., St. Louis, Missouri, was awarded a $38,000,000 fixed-price-award-fee contract for repair by replace, design build to budget demolition and construction of two new barracks facilities. Bids were solicited via the internet with 13 received. Work will be performed in Fort Gordon, Georgia, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 26, 2029. Fiscal 2027 military construction, Army funds in the amount of $38,000,000 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah, Georgia, is the contracting activity (W912HN-27-C-A004).

Amentum Services Inc., Chantilly, Virginia, was awarded a $19,852,830 modification (P00135) to contract W58RGZ-25-C-0004 for global aviation maintenance services.
